issues.failure_explanation: The lemma states a formula with I(p) in the denominator but does not assume I(p)≠0. At a real eigenvalue, I(p) can vanish (e.g., at bifurcation points). The proof only establishes the multiplied equation κκ'I = 1/2 κ²∫n'|w|². If I(p)=0, the displayed quotient is undefined unless the numerator also vanishes, in which case the derivative is not determined by the formula. Thus the statement is ill-defined as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the condition I(p)≠0 to the lemma or state the equality in the multiplied form κ_p κ_p' I(p) = 1/2 κ_p²∫ n_p'|w_p|².
issues.overall_effect: The lemma cannot be applied at points where I(p)=0 without an additional hypothesis; its use in limiting arguments requires a separate justification.
issues.title: Undefined denominator in derivative formula for I=0
issues.why_classification: A short local missing condition; adding it preserves all substantive applications and requires no new argument.

Consider an eigenpair trajectory as in \cref{prop:annulus:bifurc}, corresponding to a Bessel index $m\in\mathbb{N}_0$, i.e., the eigenfunction trajectories are as in \cref{eq:annulus:functions}, with $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$, $\delta$, and $\kappa$ being (by \cref{thm:simple}) continuous functions of $p$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof evaluates integrals of |αJ_m(κρ)+βY_m(κρ)|² using an antiderivative that requires the Bessel arguments to be real, i.e., κ real. The proposition is stated for arbitrary eigenpair trajectories, which may have complex κ. For non-real κ the Bessel functions are complex and the displayed identity is not established by the given proof.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that κ_p is real (or restrict the statement to real eigenvalue trajectories).
issues.overall_effect: The proposition is only proven for real eigenvalues; its application to non-real trajectories is unsupported as written.
issues.title: Missing reality hypothesis in annulus indicator formula
issues.why_classification: Adding the intended reality condition is a short local fix; the result is used precisely for real trajectories, so the main application survives.

issues.failure_explanation: On the annulus, v=A(ρ)φ(mθ). The bifurcation condition from \overline{I}=0 is |A(1)|² = r²|A(r)|², i.e., |A(1)| = r|A(r)|. With standard boundary L² measure, ||v||_{L²(∂B_1)} = |A(1)|√(a_mπ) and ||v||_{L²(∂B_r)} = |A(r)|√(r a_mπ). Equality of L² norms would give |A(1)| = √r |A(r)|, not |A(1)| = r|A(r)|. The missing factor √r makes the claimed equivalence false for r≠1.

failure_location.quote: By the assumed polar-coordinate separability in \cref{eq:annulus:functions}, this is actually equivalent to $\|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_1)}=\|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_r)}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the L² equality with the correct weighted equality, e.g., \|v_p\|_{L²(∂B_1)} = √r\|v_p\|_{L²(∂B_r)} (with standard surface measure), or use normalized boundary norms.
issues.overall_effect: The prose misidentifies the bifurcation condition; readers using the L² equality will obtain an incorrect criterion.
issues.title: False equivalence between L∞ and L² boundary conditions for annulus
issues.why_classification: A local algebraic correction; it does not affect the main theoretical results or the validity of the indicator formula.
